title: Nonsyndromic Genetic Hyperinsulinism Overview
result: Expert-authored, peer-reviewed overview, first posted 2003, comprehensive update 31 October 2024. GLUD1 hyperinsulinism is autosomal dominant and accounts for 42% of diazoxide-responsive hyperinsulinism with a molecular diagnosis; plasma ammonia is 1.5 to 4 times the upper limit of normal and unrelated to glucose or fasting; leucine sensitivity may occur; most patients respond to diazoxide. Diazoxide binds the ABCC8 subunit of the KATP channel, increases its probability of being open and inhibits insulin release.
